notice: Versioned public-documentation snapshot, not a live website fetch or proof of deployed API availability. API routes are reference text only; this MCP server has no account access. Guide prose and API schemas are supplemented by separately indexed canonical examples.

docs.title: Use the documentation assistant
docs.content:
# Use the documentation assistant

## What it can do

The documentation assistant is an unreleased documentation server that runs on your computer. MCP (Model Context Protocol) lets a compatible AI host discover tools supplied by a separate process. This prototype offers documentation search and reading only; it cannot retrieve accounts, inspect portfolios or execute API operations.

It reads a packaged snapshot rather than the live website. Results identify the bundle version, source checkpoint and contract hash. A route in a result is a documentation reference, not proof that an endpoint is enabled on your service. Guide prose and public operation schemas are included; guide code examples and proposal-only pages are omitted.

## Install the supplied prototype

Obtain the reviewed local archive and checksum from your integration coordinator. There is no public package installation or hosted MCP URL. The rehearsal package requires Node.js 22.12 or later in a supported LTS release; its local checks passed on Node 24.22.1. npm needs registry access to install the prototype’s dependencies; the installed server reads its packaged documentation without a network connection.

Create a separate rehearsal folder, initialize it, then install the archive with scripts disabled. Replace the path with the file you received. You do not need API credentials, an environment file or the marketing source checkout.

## Verify the installed package before connecting a host

Run this command from your rehearsal folder. It verifies the packaged snapshot and exercises local protocol initialization, tool discovery, search and reading. A successful report still says `desktopHostVerified: false`: it has not configured or tested your AI host. Resolve any startup diagnostic before continuing.

The supplied rehearsal.6 archive has SHA-256 `064e86a5aa7357a5be172607ff2f9e7c853630c97acfad83bd7cb5acb5ba6c75`. Its documentation is a frozen snapshot; the package version and documentation checkpoint are different identifiers. Check the supplied artifact receipt rather than assuming it matches the latest website.

## Use the local Claude Code or Codex plugin

Both host packages wrap the same documentation-only MCP server. They are local rehearsal packages, not a published marketplace listing or a hosted connector. The npm server, a host plugin and a remote connector are different distribution forms; publishing one does not install the others.

If you have an authorized copy of the local marketplace archive, verify its supplied checksum and extract it first. Replace the path below with the extracted root containing both marketplace manifests. Node LTS 22.12 or later must be on PATH; dependencies are bundled, so startup does not download packages. Use only the commands for your chosen host, then start a new session.

Codex tool execution has been verified for this local package. Claude Code installation was verified, but tool execution is awaiting a working Claude login. The MCP source is now public under MIT at https://github.com/bhafin/plugin. npm publication remains pending. The initial GitHub 0.1.0 installation has a dependency issue, so use only the supplied, verified rehearsal archive while the corrected public package is being verified. The commands below describe that local archive, not an installation of the initial public release.

## Connect a stdio-capable host

Use your host’s documented local-server configuration. stdio means the host starts a process and exchanges protocol messages through its standard input and output. The JSON below illustrates a common configuration shape; it is not a universal host format or an automatically installed connection.

Replace both absolute paths. Use the Node executable directly, not npm start, because npm can print banners into the protocol stream. Running the process in a terminal normally waits silently for protocol messages; silence alone does not verify a working host connection.

## Check the connection and its limits

After your host starts the process, it should discover docs_list, docs_search and docs_read. List documents, search for authentication, then read a returned document ID. Follow the returned next offset for additional pages or text; do not guess filesystem paths as document IDs.

If no tools appear, check the executable and server paths, supported Node version and your host’s process logs. If search finds nothing, try the resource or concept name; every literal search term must match. Exact document IDs or titles rank before title matches; ties retain source order. This is not semantic search. A missing document is not evidence that a product capability exists or does not exist.

Keep the bundle’s version and checkpoint in your rehearsal notes. New website changes do not update an installed archive automatically. A fresh approved archive and host restart are required to use a new snapshot. A host connection has not been verified merely because the standalone package checks pass.

docs.title: Rehearse an integration
docs.content:
# Rehearse an integration

## Choose what you are demonstrating

For an offline demonstration, install bharosa@0.1.0 from npm and use its synthetic fixtures and the documentation MCP archive. Neither needs an account connection. Label sample investors, holdings and prices as fictional; installing a fixture package does not seed a running API or populate a real account.

For a service-backed demonstration, obtain the confirmed service origin, authorized account and credentials through the operator’s established setup process. Confirm which endpoints and datasets are enabled. A method in the SDK or documentation does not establish hosted availability. Do not put credentials into slides, source files or the MCP configuration.

## Run a small, observable sequence

First check the installed SDK export, then run the synthetic samples. Separately check MCP discovery, search and reading. Record archive checksums and the returned documentation checkpoint so a later result can be traced to the same inputs.

If service access is confirmed, begin with an account read and let the person select an authorized investor and portfolio. Display dates and unavailable values alongside results. Do not begin by saving demonstration holdings into an existing account. Any write rehearsal needs a specifically designated test account and authorization for that action.

Use the exact fund plan and option selected by the person. New supplied units allow at most four fractional digits; a rounded historical display is not a new observation. When showing a snapshot total, handle null as unavailable rather than zero.

## Keep an honest fallback

If credentials, connectivity or market coverage are missing, switch back to the explicitly labeled synthetic demonstration. Do not turn a cached response into a claim that a service call succeeded. For an uncertain write response, keep the original idempotency key and reconcile its outcome before trying a new operation.

Before presenting, check the flow at a narrow viewport, keyboard navigation, readable code examples and their copy buttons. Confirm links open the intended documentation version. Keep a short list of unverified steps, such as a desktop-host connection or deployed endpoint, rather than describing them as complete.

docs.title: Latest and monthly market data
docs.content:
# Latest and monthly market data

## Before you integrate

Latest NAV and historical first-of-month market snapshots are offered to all developers without a separate market-data approval application. Use authenticated API credentials with the required account authorization. This policy does not provide anonymous API access or another person’s portfolio data. Confirm the service configuration with your integration operator; this documentation does not establish hosted availability.

Use your own account key for your server’s account integration, or the configured application key plus user authorization for an app serving others. Both are external credentials and receive the same historical market-date policy. Keep those credentials server-only.

## A month start is a cutoff, not a price date

Request historical market snapshots for the first day of a month using asOf, such as 2026-08-01. The server selects the last eligible observation on or before that day. If the latest eligible price was observed on July 31, requested_date remains August 1 and observation_date remains July 31. No future observation is selected, and future requests are rejected using today in Asia/Kolkata.

A snapshot with status missing has null data and observation_date. This is different from an available expense observation whose stored value is null. Expense ratios are normalized by the data pipeline and returned unchanged: do not multiply or divide them by 100 based on an assumed provider format. Effective dates do not prove when information was publicly available.

For a current value, omit asOf in schemes.valuation and supply recorded units. Read nav.date and freshness with the result: latest does not mean a price was observed today. You may retain latest observations over time, including daily; the monthly historical policy does not prevent that accumulation.

## Choose the right resource

Search mutualFunds for the investible scheme the user means, including its plan and option. Keep the returned scheme_id for NAV, expense and valuation calls. A fund owner is the fund whose underlying investments are disclosed; it is neither an investible scheme nor the AMC (fund house). Fund portfolio and holdings calls need that owner’s ID.

The external search example resolves scheme IDs, not a fund-owner catalogue. Obtain an owner ID through the supported data mapping in your environment before calling mutualFunds.portfolios.retrieve or mutualFunds.portfolios.holdings.list. Do not guess one from a scheme ID or copy a fictional number. A fund’s disclosed portfolio is also different from a person’s saved investment portfolio.

Holdings responses include the selected portfolio and a holdings page inside data. Keep the owner and asOf unchanged when passing holdings.next_cursor as startingAfter. Continue while has_more is true; a short page is not a completeness guarantee. This surface resolves the eligible disclosure itself and does not accept arbitrary historical portfolio IDs.

## Investor history keeps its actual dates

Monthly limits apply to historical market data for every external credential, including direct account keys. They do not restrict the dates on investor transactions, recorded positions or declared history ranges. Do not move an investor’s transaction to the first of the month to satisfy a market-data request.

Existing historical portfolio mix calculations still require exact-date NAV for valuation. They do not use the backward-as-of selection of marketSnapshots. A permitted first-of-month mix can therefore fail with historical_valuation_unavailable when no NAV exists on that exact date, including a non-trading first day. A monthly snapshot’s availability does not prove a historical mix is calculable.

Trusted internal access retains full market history through its separate interface. Neither policy supplies missing investor history, verifies ownership of user-supplied units, changes the allocation formulas, or grants data redistribution rights.

docs.title: Synthetic SDK samples
docs.content:
# Synthetic SDK samples

## Start with offline fixtures

The optional bharosa/testing export provides samplePortfolios and sampleFunds for deterministic UI tests. Importing it or calling these functions makes no network requests and needs no credentials. The main SDK entrypoint does not load these fixtures.

The scenarios use fictional synthetic: symbols and fixed January 1, 2026 dates. They are not real market instrument IDs, current prices or a calculation engine. Mapping a symbol to a real fund does not mean that fund has the fictional sample composition.

## Seeding is an explicit write

Use seedSamplePortfolio only with an authenticated account you control solely for development. Supply confirmTestAccount with the returned account ID, a stable runId, a scenario ID and an instruments mapping for every required synthetic symbol to an instrument resolved in that environment. The helper checks the account/mappings but cannot prove the account is a test environment. Never seed a customer or production account.

Nothing is seeded automatically. The helper creates reported dated snapshots, not invented transaction history or units; the empty scenario creates only an investor. Investor and portfolio creation are separate idempotent writes, not an atomic transaction. SampleSeedError.phase and investor identify the failed step and any known investor.

A lost response can follow a successful write. Retry with exactly the same account, runId, scenario and mapping; do not choose a new run ID to recover from a timeout. Changing the body under the same key can cause a conflict. Use a new run ID only when intentionally creating another sample.

docs.title: Finish your app’s sign-in setup
docs.content:
# Finish your app’s sign-in setup

## What “Sign-in setup is not complete” means

Your app’s name, website and callback URLs have been saved, but its sign-in connection has not been configured. The API calls this status `setup_required`. Registration alone does not create an application key, approve access to data, or let users connect their accounts.

There is no self-service activation button or automatic approval process yet. Repeatedly editing or registering the app will not finish sign-in setup. Keep the existing registration so its app ID and details can be used when the connection is configured.

## What you can do now

In Developer settings, open your registered app and use Edit application details to check its name, website and callback URLs. A callback URL is the exact address in your app that receives the browser after the user finishes sign-in. It must point to a route your application actually handles; do not copy another app’s callback or use a guessed address.

Use HTTPS URLs. HTTP is allowed only for local development addresses such as localhost. URLs cannot contain embedded credentials, fragments beginning with #, or wildcard hosts. Register one to ten distinct callback URLs. Keep development and production settings separate.

Prepare your app ID, intended environment, exact callback URLs and the account permissions your app needs. You can correct registration details while setup is incomplete. Do not paste secrets or user tokens into the name, website or callback fields. If a configured app needs its URLs changed, coordinate that change with the administrator so the saved details and sign-in service agree.

## What a Bharosa administrator must configure

A Bharosa administrator with access to the sign-in service must configure the app’s OAuth connection. OAuth is the process that asks a user to authorize an app to access selected account data. The configuration must agree on the app identity, exact callback addresses, target API and permitted scopes—the named permissions the app may request.

The server integration must also securely identify the app, start the user’s authorization request and deliver resulting credentials to the correct server session. An application key belongs on your server; signing a user in does not by itself authorize access to their portfolio.

This setup is currently an administrator task, not a request you can submit from this page. If you are working with a Bharosa administrator on an integration, share the non-secret details listed above through that existing coordination. Otherwise, you can prepare your registration, but cannot complete activation yourself. This documentation does not provide a support address or promise an approval timeline.

## Before you offer account connection to users

After administrator configuration, verify the connection in the intended environment: the app redirects to the registered callback, the user approves the intended account and permissions, and your server can make an authorized read. A saved registration is not evidence that those steps work.

Follow the app quickstart once you have the configured connection and credentials. The full market-history APIs remain restricted to Bharosa’s own apps. Latest NAV and monthly historical snapshots require no separate market-data approval. API authentication and account authorization still apply; finishing sign-in setup does not grant unrestricted history or permission to redistribute provider data.

docs.title: Show a family member’s saved allocation
docs.content:
# Show a family member’s saved allocation

## Choose a family, investor and portfolio

Use a configured server-side client and the account permissions described in setup. List families, let the user choose one, then list its investors and select a person. Names are display labels, not unique IDs. Filter saved portfolios by the selected investor and let the user choose the portfolio.

The select callback belongs to your app’s UI, not the SDK. It must return an ID from the supplied choices. Finish pagination before presenting the complete selection.

## Keep the snapshot date visible

This calculation uses the latest saved snapshot values; it does not reprice units with today’s NAV. Show the snapshot and underlying source dates alongside allocation. Use the resource reference to inspect market dates separately; a price observation does not verify ownership.

docs.title: Introduction
docs.content:
# Introduction

## A clear model for investment data

Bharosa gives your application a consistent way to read and record investment data. You can organize a person’s portfolios, keep family members’ investments separate, and connect each position to a specific mutual fund instrument.

Start with an account: every request is checked against the account your credentials are allowed to access. Within that account, a Client groups people, an Investor represents one person, and a Portfolio groups that investor’s investment records. A Client here is a group such as a family; it is not the application you are building.

A portfolio’s name and owner are separate from its positions. A position describes the quantity or value of an instrument on a particular date. A holding gives that investment a continuing identity within a portfolio and investment account, so that observations and transactions can refer to it over time.

## Build with HTTP or TypeScript

Choose HTTP requests or the TypeScript SDK to call the same resource API from your server. The SDK supplies typed methods; it does not grant additional permissions or change the meaning of the data.

For a server integration accessing your own account, use a direct account key. If you are building an app for other users, use a delegated application key together with each user’s OAuth access token and account authorization. Signing in alone does not give an app access to portfolio data.

The quickstart offers setup paths for your own account and for an app serving other users. Both begin with a read-only account request. You will need an assigned service origin and authorized credentials before running it. All names, IDs and values in the examples are fictional; replace them with records returned by your configured service.

## India mutual funds, with context intact

The historical manual portfolio workflow supports India mutual funds with values entered in INR. Each save records a dated snapshot: a fixed set of positions and their reported values. A later save creates another snapshot rather than editing the old one.

Fund reference data helps you identify a scheme and display its net asset value (NAV), or value per unit, on a stated date. Refreshing a reference does not recalculate the values entered in a manual snapshot. A snapshot total is the sum of those entered values, not an investment return or a measure of all the investor’s wealth.

docs.title: Quickstart
docs.content:
# Quickstart

## Choose your setup

Bharosa has one resource API and one TypeScript SDK. The setup differs according to whose account your code accesses. Once configured, both clients use the same methods to read accounts, investors and portfolios.

The setup examples check required environment variables before any request. A missing value produces an error naming the variable, never its contents. Supply it through your server configuration; do not replace missing credentials with sample values. Keep credentials on your server. Both paths require an assigned service origin and authorized access; visiting this documentation does not create an account, register an application or enable a data provider.

## Work with your own account

For a script or server workload accessing an account you control, configure a direct account key. Start with a read-only account request before adding portfolio writes.

## Build an app for other users

For a third-party application, configure an application key together with each user’s authorized account and access token. The resource API supports this delegated context. Establishing the external connection flow still requires trusted server integration; there is no general self-service Connect Bharosa entrypoint available.

## Continue with the shared reference

After either setup, use the same resource methods. TypeScript reference snippets continue after the configured bharosa client. cURL examples include the credential headers for the selected setup.

docs.title: An app for other users
docs.content:
# An app for other users

## Establish the connection integration first

The Developer settings form records an app’s details. The status `setup_required` means Bharosa must still configure its OAuth connection; registration creates no key, approval or access grant. Developers cannot yet offer a ready-made “Connect Bharosa” flow to their users. The steps below describe the required integration once that connection is configured.

The connection flow has been implemented and tested locally with synthetic accounts and a simulated identity provider. It is not enabled on the hosted service. Real-provider configuration, production wiring, database rollout and HTTPS browser verification must be completed before an external app can use it. Local test results do not grant access or make this a self-service connection option.

Before an external app can connect users, its registration, authenticated app sessions, consent initiation and secure token delivery need a trusted server integration. Do not substitute Bharosa’s browser sign-in routes or a user-entered account ID for that integration.

## What your server needs

Have the assigned HTTPS API origin, a registered application, and its secret application key. For each user, obtain the account ID and API access token from that user’s validated authorization grant for the same application. A sign-in ID token is not an API access token.

The first request below needs accounts:read. The application policy, key, token and active grant must all permit that scope. The application key alone gives no access to any account.

The TypeScript examples use the published `bharosa@0.1.0` npm package with Node.js 22.12 or later in a supported LTS release. Follow the SDK installation guide before running them. Keep keys, tokens and grant records on the server. Create a separate immutable client for each user grant.

## Configure a client for one authorized user

For this server-only example, set BHAROSA_APPLICATION_KEY, BHAROSA_API_BASE_URL, BHAROSA_ACCOUNT_ID and BHAROSA_USER_ACCESS_TOKEN from trusted configuration and one validated grant. In a multi-user app, select the grant from the authenticated server session, never from untrusted browser input.

The response contains the account authorized by that grant. Both onboarding paths now use the same resource methods: the invocation below is identical to the own-account request.

## Make the same request over HTTP

Send both headers. Authorization identifies the application key; Bharosa-User-Authorization carries the user’s access token. Use the account selected in that grant. A successful request returns 200 OK and the account object.

## Resolve access failures before continuing

For 401, check both credentials and token expiry. Refresh only through the validated server lifecycle when a refresh token was issued; revoked or invalid grants require fresh authorization. Do not retry unchanged credentials indefinitely.

For 403, check the grant’s account and the permissions shared by the application policy, key and token. Additional scopes need explicit authorization. Once the read succeeds, continue with the shared reference or first-portfolio walkthrough; fund lookup also requires an available authorized market-data provider.

docs.title: Your own account
docs.content:
# Your own account

## Before you begin

This walkthrough first reads your account and its investors without changing any data. Have an existing Bharosa account, its account ID, an assigned API service origin, and a direct account key for that account. A scope is a named permission: accounts:read permits the account request, and investors:read permits the investor list.

For the portfolio workflow that follows, also obtain clients:read and portfolios:read. Saving a portfolio requires portfolios:write. Fund lookup requires an available, authorized market-data provider. Documentation access does not itself provision an API account or activate that provider.

Store BHAROSA_SECRET_KEY, BHAROSA_ACCOUNT_ID and BHAROSA_API_BASE_URL in your server environment. Use the supplied HTTPS service origin without a trailing slash, path, query, fragment or embedded credentials. The fictional key shown elsewhere in these docs will not authenticate.

The SDK examples use the published `bharosa@0.1.0` npm package and Node.js 22.12 or later in a supported LTS release. Follow the SDK installation guide before running them. You can also use the HTTP example below. For an app serving other users, complete the OAuth setup first instead of substituting their account ID into this direct-key example.

## Initialize your server client

Create a client on your server with the service origin, account ID and direct account key. The two calls below retrieve the account and the first ten investor profiles. Keep the key out of browser bundles, mobile apps, source control, URLs and logs.

On success, account contains the authorized account’s details, while investors.data contains the profiles you can select for a portfolio. Keep the IDs returned by the API; the example IDs in this documentation do not identify your records.

## Make the same request over HTTP

If you prefer HTTP, this cURL command makes the same account retrieval request. It should return 200 OK with an account object. All resource paths start with /v1; changing the account in the path does not change what your key is allowed to access.

If you receive 401, check that the key is present, valid and unexpired. A 403 response means the credentials do not authorize the requested operation or account. Resolve those conditions before adding write operations to your integration.

## Save your first holdings

Once the read requests succeed, choose an investor from investors.data and follow the first-portfolio guide. You will search for a fund instrument, submit an entered current value, and receive a snapshot containing the saved positions and their total.

Keep the returned `snapshot.id` when you open an editor. The next save uses that ID to detect whether someone else has updated the portfolio in the meantime.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.content:
# Authentication

## Authentication versus authorization

Choose credentials according to whose account your code will access. “Your own account” examples use a direct account key: a secret assigned to a server workload you control, with access to one account. Send it in Authorization: Bearer <secret API key>.

Each key has named permissions called scopes. For example, portfolios:read permits reading portfolio data, while portfolios:write is needed to save it. The API checks both the account and the operation’s required scope. Replacing an account ID in the URL never expands a key’s access.

## Acting for a user

Choose “An app for other users” when a registered application needs to access accounts on its users’ behalf. This is delegated access. The application has its own key, and each user separately authorizes access to a selected account through OAuth.

Send the application key in Authorization: Bearer <key> and the user’s access token in Bharosa-User-Authorization: Bearer <access token>. Both credentials must belong to the same registered application, and the selected account must match the active user grant. The application key alone grants no account access, even to the application owner’s account.

The API allows only permissions shared by the key, token, active grant and application policy. Do not pair a direct account key with a user token. Invalid supplied credentials are rejected rather than silently treated as another authentication mode.

OpenID Connect sign-in identifies a user. OAuth consent authorizes data access. An ID token from sign-in is not an API access token, and signing in does not by itself authorize your application to read a portfolio.

## Respond to access failures

401 means authentication is missing, expired or invalid. Reauthenticate or replace the invalid credential; do not loop requests unchanged. 403 means the authenticated caller lacks permission: request the specific scope or account consent.

404 resource_missing is used for missing or foreign-account resources. Do not probe other account IDs or infer existence from authorization failures.

docs.title: API keys
docs.content:
# API keys

## Choose the smallest useful scope

Read scopes are accounts:read, clients:read, investors:read and portfolios:read. Mutation scopes are investors:write and portfolios:write. Fund search and references use portfolios:read.

Choose the key type explicitly. A direct account key is bound to one account-owned workload. A delegated application key is bound to an OAuth application and a scope ceiling, with no direct access to the application owner’s or any other account. Separate credentials by environment and workload. A family profile is data, not permission to act as that family member.

## Store and use keys safely

Inject secrets through your server environment or secret store. Do not use browser-exposed environment-variable prefixes. Redact authorization headers, cookies and tokens from request logs.

In signed-in Developer settings, choose a registered target, explicit permissions and expiry. A new secret is shown once. If creation or rotation has an uncertain outcome, refresh the key list before another change. A lost secret cannot be recovered; reconcile the listed key, revoke it and create a replacement rather than retrying blindly.

The literal bh_sk_FICTIONAL_DO_NOT_USE is only a documentation placeholder. Do not embed it as a working fallback.

## Rotate and revoke

Rotation creates a replacement while both keys remain active until expiry or explicit revocation. Update dependent deployments, verify access using an operation permitted by the key’s scopes, then explicitly revoke the old key. Rotation alone does not secure a compromised key.

If a key is exposed, revoke it promptly, replace it, and review access. Revocation removes application-key access; OAuth grant revocation independently removes delegated user access. Never store credentials in idempotency keys.

docs.title: OAuth & user authorization
docs.content:
# OAuth & user authorization

## A consent-based authorization flow

Use a confidential server application or a browser application backed by your server. An app running entirely in a browser or on a user’s device cannot keep an application secret; direct browser/mobile token handling requires a separately registered public-client integration. Account-key and delegated SDK configuration is server-only.

The Developer settings form records application details only. A `setup_required` status means the OAuth connection still needs to be configured by Bharosa; it does not mean the app is ready to connect users. Once that integration is established, use its exact registered redirect URI, required scopes and configured authorization and token endpoints. Initiate the authorization-code flow with state and PKCE; retain the verifier on the initiating session.

The user signs in and chooses the account and requested permissions to grant. On callback, validate state, exchange the code with the original redirect URI and verifier, and bind the returned grant to that user session. Reject callbacks that do not match an initiated transaction.

Bharosa’s /auth/login and /auth/callback routes belong to its browser sign-in flow. They are not portfolio resource endpoints or substitutes for an application’s registered redirect URI.

## Send delegated context from your server

Keep tokens server-side. Initialize the SDK with auth.type delegated_application, its apiKey and userAccessToken; account must be the grant’s account ID. Do not trust an account ID supplied by the browser as authorization.

The access token authorizes data access; an ID token identifies a signed-in user and must not be sent as a data API access token.

## Expiry, consent and revocation

Respect token expiry and granted scopes. Use a refresh token only when one was issued and store any rotated replacement atomically. On `invalid_grant` or revoked consent, stop delegated requests and ask the user to reconnect.

Logout ends the browser session; it does not disconnect the OAuth grant. Disconnect immediately revokes local account access and requests provider refresh-family revocation. Provider completion can remain pending. Active grants are checked on every API request, including idempotent replay.

Developer settings distinguishes Connected, Delivery pending, Reconnect required, Revoked and Provider revocation pending. Provider revocation pending means local access is already revoked. Retry provider revocation explicitly retries upstream cleanup without restoring local access; refreshing the list alone does not retry it. Reconnect requires fresh approval. A new browser login requires reconnect for that browser-bound integration.

Refresh connection recovers an existing pending server delivery before requesting another refresh. Tokens stay server-side. An uncertain provider exchange requires fresh consent; do not replay its callback or treat sign-in as approval.

Do not broaden permissions silently. Additional scopes or a different account require explicit authorization. Disconnecting an application revokes its grant; retaining a secret application key does not preserve delegated access.

docs.title: Accounts & resources
docs.content:
# Accounts & resources

## Resource definitions

An Account is the access boundary for the records in these docs. Its id identifies the account, and primary_investor may identify a profile or be null. The public response does not expose the internal owner user ID. Its optional name is a display label and can differ from the owner’s name.

personal_client_id is the authenticated person’s household group in this account. Machine account keys return null; a missing personal link also returns null. The schema permits omission, which provides no context. This is not a membership grant or a user directory. accounts.retrieve() uses your configured account, so no repeated account ID is needed. If there is no personal client, let the caller select an authorized client rather than guessing from a name or primary investor.

A Client groups investors within an account, for example under “My family.” Its account field links it to that account. This use of Client is unrelated to an OAuth application or SDK client, and creating a family profile does not grant anyone login access.

An Investor represents a person. Its client and account fields identify where the profile belongs. relationship_to_owner is self, spouse, child, parent, sibling or other. Use the investor ID for requests because two people can have the same name.

A Portfolio belongs to an investor and stores metadata such as name and reporting_currency. Retrieve its current snapshot separately to obtain positions and values. That separation lets you read a portfolio’s identity without assuming its current holdings are embedded in the metadata response.

## Opaque IDs and ownership

Normal resource IDs use a type prefix and 32 lowercase hexadecimal characters: acct_, clt_, inv_, ptf_, iac_, psn_ and pos_. Treat all identifiers as opaque; instrument identifiers can be catalogue-specific.

The account alias me resolves the authorized account context. It is not a way to enumerate another user’s accounts. Client filters organize records within existing permission boundaries.

## Representing a family

One self investor represents the owner. Create additional profiles in the same family Client and save each portfolio with its investor ID. Adding an investor does not invite them or create shared login access.

A Client association is fixed on investor creation. Select the family explicitly when there is more than one Client; never infer it from the first list result or a matching name.

docs.title: Portfolios & snapshots
docs.content:
# Portfolios & snapshots

## The snapshot response

A portfolio groups an investor’s investments. Its investment account is the container in which holdings are recorded; in history workflows this can distinguish separate folios. A holding identifies one asset within that portfolio and investment account. A position describes what was observed or reconstructed for the holding on a date.

For manual portfolios, a snapshot records the complete set of entered positions at one effective date. The response includes portfolio and investment_account metadata, the snapshot revision, and positions. investment_account.latest_snapshot points to the currently selected revision.

Each position links an instrument to the snapshot. Amount-based entries contain a reported INR valuation and unknown quantity. The unreleased units-first creation path stores a positive quantity with null valuation; it does not invent an amount. cost_basis remains null. The instruments collection preserves the reference metadata attached when the snapshot was saved.

Read `total_current_value` for the exact sum of entered values and `snapshot.as_of` for their effective date. Amount-only snapshots use manual_current_value. If any position contains only supplied units, the total is null and valuation_basis is supplied_quantity: unavailable is not zero. The separate market_data field describes reference data; it does not turn an entered value into a calculated return.

## Interpret missing values correctly

Null quantity and cost mean unknown, not zero. A current value does not imply units, purchase price, profit or tax cost. Do not divide by NAV to fabricate quantity.

created is ingestion time in Unix seconds. as_of is the financial date with Asia/Kolkata context. Reference NAV has its own date, which may differ from the holdings date.

## A complete set on every save

`current_snapshot` selects the latest revision and is mutable. Each returned snapshot and its pinned instrument metadata are immutable. Snapshot IDs are revision tokens; this interface does not expose history retrieval by ID.

A replacement publishes all supported positions in one snapshot. Omit a fund to remove it. Send positions: [] to clear holdings. Previous snapshots remain immutable.

Use expected_snapshot to prevent a stale editor overwriting a newer save. Same-date corrections are allowed; older effective dates cannot replace newer holdings.

docs.title: Decimal money & dates
docs.content:
# Decimal money & dates

## Decimal strings, not floating-point numbers

Send current_value as a nonnegative plain decimal string, with at most 20 integer digits and 18 fractional digits. Examples: "0", "125000.50", "2456.789". Do not send numbers, commas, exponents, NaN or negative values.

Amounts are in INR major units. The canonical response may remove trailing zeroes, so "125000.50" and "125000.5" have the same value. Use a decimal library for arithmetic and formatting; do not round before submission. Totals can exceed a single position’s bound.

## Keep financial dates explicit

Use a real YYYY-MM-DD calendar date in Asia/Kolkata, from 1900-01-01 through today. Same-date corrections create a new snapshot; a replacement cannot move the effective date backward.

An as_of object with precision date retains date and time_zone. Do not convert a date-only observation into an invented UTC instant. created is a Unix-second ingestion timestamp, not financial freshness.

docs.title: Pagination
docs.content:
# Pagination

## Request the next page

Client, investor and portfolio lists return a page at a time. Omit `starting_after` for the first request and choose limit from 1 to 100; the default is 10. The response’s data array contains that page’s records.

If `has_more` is true, request the next page using the last data item’s ID as `starting_after` and keep the same filters. The SDK spells this option startingAfter. Stop when `has_more` is false. The returned url is the resource path, not a saved copy of your query filters.

Fund search and exact reference lookup have their own result limits and do not use these cursors. Multiple list requests are not a frozen view: records can change while you are moving through pages.

## Ordering and recovery

In the reviewed local SDK, malformed resource pages throw `InvalidResponseError`: duplicate IDs within a page, an empty page claiming more results, the incoming exclusive cursor appearing again, or more records than requested. Do not treat that failure as an empty successful list. Your multi-page loop should also track seen IDs and cursors, stop on overlap or cycles, and show a recoverable error rather than silently dropping records.

Lists are newest first, with descending ID as the tie-breaker. Cursor ordering uses full stored creation precision even when created is returned in seconds.

A missing, foreign-account or out-of-filter cursor returns 400 invalid_cursor. Restart with the intended filters and deduplicate by ID if records changed during traversal. A multi-page walk is not a frozen account-wide snapshot.

docs.title: Idempotency
docs.content:
# Idempotency

## One key per logical operation

Send Idempotency-Key for investor creation, portfolio creation and snapshot replacement. Investor updates also accept a key; use one whenever the request might be retried. An investor profile update is a partial update with last-write-wins fields; snapshot updates instead require expected_snapshot. Generate a unique key per new operation, for example with crypto.randomUUID().

Reuse the same key only with the same account, method, route and JSON body after a timeout or retryable failure. Object key ordering is ignored; array ordering and decimal-string spelling are significant. A changed body under the same key returns a conflict. Never use a person’s name, credentials or account data as the key.

## Understand the replay window

Successful responses are retained for 24 hours from when the server records the successful response. The record and mutation commit atomically; retries do not extend retention. Every retry rechecks current credential, account, scope and grant authorization before replay. An authorized identical retry returns the original result, even if a newer snapshot now exists; it does not refresh NAV.

After that window, reconcile current resources before resubmitting an uncertain write. A new key can create a new operation. Validation and conflict errors need corrective action, not blind repetition.

docs.title: Errors & recovery
docs.content:
# Errors & recovery

## The error envelope

When a request fails, read the error object before deciding whether to retry. type is the broad category, code identifies the condition, and message explains it. param points to the relevant input when one is available.

Keep request_id and the HTTP status in diagnostic logs so you can trace a failed request. Leave credentials and personal request bodies out of those logs. The example below shows a save rejected because the snapshot changed while an editor was open.

## Choose the right recovery

A 400 response usually needs a corrected request. For invalid_cursor, restart the list with the intended filters. For invalid_instruments, check the exact instrument IDs and remove duplicates. Repeating the same invalid request will not fix it.

For 401, replace missing, expired or invalid credentials. For 403, obtain the required scope or account authorization. A 404 resource_missing means the record is missing or is not accessible in the selected account; verify the account and ID instead of probing other accounts.

A 409 response needs attention to the specific conflict. For snapshot_conflict, fetch the current snapshot and reconcile it with the user’s draft. For self_investor_exists, retrieve the existing self profile. For an idempotency conflict, compare the body with the original request; use a new key only if you intend a new operation.

The local history-import implementation has a 30-second service budget. A timeout or disconnected client before commit cancels the import transaction; after commit starts, the result can be uncertain. Preserve the original body and idempotency key to reconcile the outcome. Cancellation is not a promise that nothing was saved, and it does not prove that upstream read-only work stopped immediately.

For 429, honor Retry-After when present. For a network timeout or transient 502, 503 or 504, retry a limited number of times with increasing, randomized delays. Preserve the original body and idempotency key for writes. A timeout means the outcome is unknown, not necessarily that the save failed.

If market_data_unavailable is returned with 503, keep the saved holdings visible and retry the reference lookup later. An unavailable reference must not become an invented price or erase the user’s data.

## Keep retries bounded

409 request_in_progress means another attempt with the same key is still running; retry that unchanged request within your retry budget. Do not automatically retry other conflicts or all 4xx responses. Cap transient retries and show a recoverable failure state. Never replace a failed reference lookup with invented prices or hide saved holdings because the market provider is unavailable.

docs.title: Build your first portfolio
docs.content:
# Build your first portfolio

## 1. Select the investor and fund

Begin with the configured server client from either onboarding path. Retrieve the account, list its investors, and select the person whose portfolio you want to create. Use that persisted investor ID rather than a name or a fictional ID from an example.

Next, search mutual funds using at least two characters and let the user choose a resolved instrument. Show the scheme, plan and option together. Fund lookup and saving need available, authorized market-reference data; if lookup returns 503, retain the draft and retry later instead of guessing an instrument ID.

## 2. Submit the initial positions

The request below illustrates a portfolio with its initial positions. Replace the fictional investor and instrument IDs with your selections. Supply a portfolio name, an effective date in the India calendar, and 1–100 distinct instruments with user-entered INR values. Send each `current_value` as a decimal string. Units-first creation is implemented locally but not released: each position may instead supply a positive quantity decimal string with at most four fractional digits, never both quantity and current_value. The same as_of date records when the units were observed. A NAV is not required to save them. Snapshot replacement still requires amounts.

Generate one idempotency key for this intended save. It identifies the operation if a connection fails and you need to retry. Keep that key and the unchanged request body until you know the outcome; a new key represents a new operation.

## Create from units you already know

This path is not released yet. After choosing the investor and exact fund instrument, record a positive unit count with at most four fractional digits and its observation date. Five fractional digits are rejected even if the last digit is zero; input is not silently rounded. These are fictional placeholders: replace both IDs with the records selected above. Do not infer units from a guessed price or supply an invented amount.

The save does not need a NAV. In its snapshot response, `quantity` contains the supplied units and `valuation` is null. If any position has no reported amount, `total_current_value` is null and `valuation_basis` is `supplied_quantity`. Display an unavailable value rather than zero. This does not calculate a current NAV valuation or change snapshot-replacement inputs.

## 3. Display the result

A successful creation returns 201 Created with the portfolio and its first snapshot. Display result.positions and `total_current_value` together with `snapshot.as_of`, so the user can see the date the entered values describe. Handle a null total explicitly when units-only positions are present.

Keep `snapshot.id` for the next edit. When the page reloads, retrieve `current_snapshot` to recover the saved positions; retrieving portfolio metadata alone will not return them. If you also show a reference NAV, label it with its own date and freshness instead of using it to silently replace the entered values.

docs.title: Add a family member
docs.content:
# Add a family member

## 1. Resolve the family Client

A family member is another investor profile within the account, not another authorized login. Read personal_client_id from the authorized account to identify the authenticated person’s linked family, when present. For machine keys or missing context, have the caller deliberately select an existing authorized Client; do not infer a personal family from a self investor, name or list order. Request investors:write for profile creation.

Do not assume the first Client in a list is the family, or that primary_investor always identifies it. Choose the intended existing Client explicitly before submitting the request.

## 2. Create the profile

Send the person’s name, relationship to the owner and the family Client ID. This stores a profile, not a user invitation or delegated authorization.

## 3. Associate their portfolio

Use member.id in the portfolio creation request. Render lists grouped by portfolio.investor. Names can repeat, so use IDs for all selection and update operations.

docs.title: Build fund autocomplete
docs.content:
# Build fund autocomplete

## Search as the user types

A person invests in a particular scheme, plan and option, not just a fund name. For example, Direct and Regular plans or Growth and distribution options must remain distinguishable in your selector. The API returns an instrument identity for the exact choice.

Search after the user has entered at least two characters, with limit between 1 and 20. Debounce input and ignore responses for older queries so a slow response cannot replace the latest results. Send the request through your server to keep credentials out of the browser.

The search relevance update is not yet released. It puts exact identifier and name matches ahead of name prefixes, whole-word matches and broader matches. Numeric terms remain distinct: a search for 50 should prefer that token over 500. Results still require the user to choose the intended plan and option; do not automatically select the first match.

When a query ends with an explicit catalogue plan and optional option, such as Regular Growth or Direct Growth, the local ranking update uses those labels to distinguish matching rows while ranking the base fund name. Omitting an option does not choose Growth for you, and omitting a plan does not default to Direct. Keep meaningful words such as Growth in the fund name; always confirm the returned scheme, plan and option before selection.

The local, unreleased search also separates copied punctuation such as commas, parentheses and slashes into terms. You can paste a complete scheme label while retaining Direct or Regular and Growth or IDCW. This is not typo correction or abbreviation expansion: check spelling and use the full name when shorthand finds nothing. Short fragments may produce broader matches, so always confirm the exact plan and option.

A search failure is a failed read, not evidence that a portfolio save occurred. Keep the entered draft and any saved holdings, explain that search is temporarily unavailable, and offer Retry fund search. Do not replace a failed request with an empty-results message or choose a similar scheme automatically.

Show the scheme name, plan_label and option_label together. An empty data array means there are no matching results. Allow selection only when identity_status is resolved; a conflicting identity is not safe to use for a save.

## Persist identity, not a label

Use the selected instrument.id in portfolio positions and save it alongside the entered current value. scheme_id, AMFI code, ISIN and display labels describe the reference but are not substitutes for instrument.id in those requests.

The SDK also exposes a MutualFund calculation handle. Its owner ID identifies the fund that owns the underlying investment portfolio; it is neither the asset management company (AMC) nor the investible scheme ID. When starting from a discovered instrument, use fromInstrument rather than guessing or converting an owner ID.

When reopening an editor, resolve the saved instrument IDs with the exact references endpoint. The missing array reports IDs that could not be resolved. Keep the saved position and show the unavailable reference instead of replacing it with a similarly named scheme.

## Treat NAV as reference data

Show latest_nav only when non-null, including its date. Show unavailable or stale states explicitly. Reference refreshes must not change manual holdings, quantity, or totals.

docs.title: Correct or update holdings
docs.content:
# Correct or update holdings

## 1. Load the current snapshot

Open the editor by retrieving `current_snapshot`. Copy all its positions into the draft and retain `snapshot.id` as expected_snapshot. This revision tells the API which version the user started editing. Keep monetary amounts as decimal strings throughout the form and request.

## 2. Send the complete set

A replacement sends the complete desired position list, not just the changed rows. Omit an instrument to remove it, or send an empty list to clear the portfolio. The request accepts 0–100 distinct instruments. Use the same effective date to correct that date’s values, or a later India date to record new values.

Include expected_snapshot and one new idempotency key for this edit. On success, update the editor with the returned positions and `snapshot.id`. The old snapshot remains unchanged, while `current_snapshot` now selects the new revision.

## 3. Reconcile conflicts

If another save wins, keep the user’s draft and fetch the newest snapshot. Compare old, draft and current values before asking the user to resolve differences. Do not merely swap expected_snapshot and resend.

docs.title: Handle stale edits & retries
docs.content:
# Handle stale edits & retries

## When the response is lost

A timeout does not prove the write failed. Retry the identical request with the original idempotency key within the 24-hour retention window. This recovers the original successful response when one exists.

## When a newer edit exists

409 snapshot_conflict means expected_snapshot no longer matches. Fetch `current_snapshot`, preserve the draft, and reconcile changed funds and values.

After the user confirms the reconciled complete set, submit the current snapshot ID and a new idempotency key. Blindly retrying the old body can overwrite someone else’s intended correction.

## When the retry window has passed

Read current holdings and compare with the intended operation before sending anything again. Show an uncertain-outcome state if the result cannot be established. A fresh key starts a new operation.

docs.title: Understand NAV freshness
docs.content:
# Understand NAV freshness

## What recent means

latest_nav is nullable. When present it contains amount, currency INR and date. freshness.status recent means its date is at most three Asia/Kolkata calendar days old. It does not guarantee the latest published NAV or a refresh SLA.

freshness.checked_at is the UTC instant when the API evaluated freshness. as_of is the India date used for that evaluation; age_days is calendar-day age, and recent_within_days is 3. These are not vendor ingestion timestamps.

## Handle every state

recent: display the NAV and date. stale: retain its date and indicate age. missing: show unavailable rather than zero. invalid: withhold the value; invalid dates, nonpositive amounts or wrong currency are not usable NAV. fixture identifies illustrative reference data.

Exact resolution returns missing IDs separately. Preserve saved holdings when a reference is missing or the provider returns 503. Retry lookup separately; do not rewrite snapshot instruments.

## NAV does not revalue manual holdings

Entered `current_value` is independent of reference NAV. Refreshing a fund does not change snapshot totals, quantities or cost basis. This interface supplies dated references, not historical NAV series or calculated returns.

docs.title: TypeScript SDK
docs.content:
# TypeScript SDK

## Install the TypeScript SDK

The TypeScript SDK is published on npm as `bharosa@0.1.0`. Use Node.js 22.12 or later in a supported LTS release. Installing the package does not provision an account or enable API access.

In a new backend project, install the pinned version below from npm. Install scripts are disabled. Pinning the version keeps your initial integration on the release documented here.

The commands below work in a project using the installed npm package. Contributor commands such as scripts/check-local-examples.mjs require the SDK source checkout and its development tooling; they are not installed-package commands. Use the linked synthetic samples for an offline application example.

The import check should print Bharosa export: function without making an API request. The final command runs the packaged synthetic smoke example and should print Installed SDK synthetic smoke passed. No network or persisted writes. It needs no account or key; it does not verify service access. After it passes, choose your account or delegated setup below. For an offline rehearsal, use the synthetic samples guide instead of supplying live credentials.

## One client, one account context

The SDK turns the HTTP operations into typed methods on a Bharosa client. Create it on your server with baseUrl, account and auth. Choose auth.type account_key for your own account, or delegated_application for an app serving another user. The latter requires both apiKey and userAccessToken.

Keep one immutable client per delegated user grant. Do not switch the account or token on a shared client between requests: each client should retain the credentials and account belonging to that grant.

The request and response models keep the API’s snake_case field names. SDK request options use names such as startingAfter for the HTTP `starting_after` cursor and `idempotencyKey` for the Idempotency-Key header. Annotate an investor creation body with InvestorCreate when storing it in a variable so TypeScript preserves the allowed relationship choices.

Requests accept only documented enum values. Responses may add new category strings over time; preserve an unfamiliar value and show an appropriate fallback instead of interpreting it as a known category. Object and resource-type discriminators remain strict.

## Resource methods

Begin with accounts.retrieve() to read the authorized account. Use clients.list() and investors.list() to find the group and person for a portfolio. Each resource also supports retrieve(id); investors additionally supports create(body, options) and update(id, body, options).

Use mutualFunds.search({ query, limit }) to help a user select an instrument, then mutualFunds.references({ instruments }) to resolve exact saved instrument IDs. To save a portfolio, call portfolios.create(body, options). List or retrieve portfolios for their metadata, and use snapshots.retrieveCurrent(id) for their current positions. snapshots.create(id, body, options) saves a complete replacement.

For a calculation without saving, portfolios.build({ valuationDate, positions }) creates an in-memory portfolio. fromPositions is an equivalent alias. The supplied positions and their entries are copied and frozen; changing your original array will not change the handle. Use portfolios.create when you intend to persist records.

Both saved and in-memory portfolios expose assetMix(), sectorMix() and issuerMix(). Saved portfolios also expose currentSnapshot() and use their current snapshot for these calculations. The optional { `asOf` } selects the underlying funds’ holdings date cutoff; it does not rewind the investor’s positions.

A MutualFund handle represents the fund that owns an underlying portfolio. Use mutualFunds.fromId(ownerId) only with that owner ID, or fromInstrument(instrumentId) when starting from an investible instrument. The fund.portfolio property is a calculation handle, not a downloaded list of holdings. Scheme IDs and AMC IDs are different identities and cannot be substituted for owner IDs.

These calculations support India INR mutual-fund portfolios. Asset mix uses signed net exposure, so negative values or percentages above 100 can be valid. Sector and issuer mixes normalize equity contributions only, rather than describing the whole portfolio. Inspect source dates, warnings and reported precision before displaying results. Nonempty underlying holdings with zero net value produce an error.

Calculations are read-only server calls and do not require an idempotency key. Mutations use { `idempotencyKey` } in request options. The SDK does not obtain new user consent or resolve concurrent-edit conflicts for you. API access is not open for general use yet.

## Observed positions and declared history

Use holding history when you need to answer what an investor held on a date, rather than only showing the latest manual snapshot. A holding belongs to a portfolio, an investment account or folio, and an asset. Two folios holding the same asset remain separate holdings; closed holdings remain available for historical queries.

After retrieving a saved portfolio, use holdings.list() to discover its holding IDs and holdings.retrieve(id) to obtain a handle. history.retrieve() returns the recorded observations, opening quantities, transactions and declarations. history.import(body, options) adds supported history, while history.canReconstruct(date) checks whether the portfolio has the required support for that date.

An observation is evidence for one particular date. holding.positionOn(date) returns an exact observation when present, even if its quantity is null because only a value was recorded. A later opening balance does not hide an earlier exact observation. An observation on one date is never silently carried backward to fill a missing date.

For other dates, reconstruction needs an opening quantity, buy/sell transactions, and a declared complete range. The opening is the quantity at the start of its date. Daily close includes that day’s transactions in their explicit sequence order. The investment account owns the timezone, which defaults to Asia/Kolkata. An opening balance is not recorded as an invented purchase.

A complete range is a statement by the source or user that the necessary history was supplied. It retains provenance and is not independent certification. Reconciling quantities alone does not create completeness. position_backing tells you whether evidence comes from snapshots, a transaction ledger, or both; it is separate from the completeness claim.

For dated portfolio calculations, call portfolio.on(`positionDate`), then assetMix(), sectorMix() or issuerMix(). The position date selects the investor’s holdings. valuationDate selects the date used to value them, and `asOf` selects the underlying funds’ holdings cutoff. Pass { valuationDate, `asOf` } to the mix method when those dates differ. Valuation defaults to `positionDate` and needs an existing provider NAV for that exact date; there is no stale-price or currency-conversion fallback.

Strict portfolio reconstruction needs a declared portfolio range and support for every stored holding, including closed holdings. history_unavailable and history_incomplete explain missing history support. External historical market dates must be month starts even with an account key; investor transaction and position dates remain unrestricted. historical_valuation_unavailable means the exact NAV needed for valuation is unavailable. An in-memory value-only portfolio cannot reconstruct earlier dates, and a fund calculation handle does not support investor dated views.

Imports require portfolios:write and an idempotency key. Within a source, transaction external_id identifies an event: replay applies it once and a conflicting payload fails. A later import may extend the same declared range forward, but cannot move its start or shrink it. Importing transactions alone preserves the existing declaration’s provenance.

New quantities use decimal strings with at most 20 whole digits and four fractional places; excess precision is rejected rather than rounded. Previously stored historical evidence retains its exact precision (up to 18 fractional places) in reads and calculations. A display rounded to four places is an approximation, not replacement evidence. Valuation fails explicitly if the result cannot be represented with the supported precision. An import is limited to 100 holdings and 5,000 transactions per holding. Transfers, splits, reversals, corrections, tax lots, performance calculations and public price imports are not supported. Neither the holding-history API nor the SDK package is publicly released yet.

## A small history example

Suppose a statement records 10 units at the start of 1 January 2026 and a buy of 3 units on 3 January. If the source declares the range 1–31 January complete, the supported daily-close position on 10 January is 13 units. The import example uses those fictional values; replace its portfolio, investment account and instrument IDs with your own records.

Import that history once with an idempotency key, retrieve it to confirm the stored source and range, then check history.canReconstruct("2026-01-10"). Use holding.positionOn("2026-01-10") for one holding. Without a complete range, those transactions do not establish that no other activity occurred: reconstruction is unavailable except where an exact observed position supplies point evidence.

For a portfolio mix, imagine asking for positions on 10 January, valuing them using 12 January NAVs, and selecting underlying fund holdings no later than 31 December. Use portfolio.on("2026-01-10") with { valuationDate: "2026-01-12", asOf: "2025-12-31" } on the mix method. These are three separate questions. All required investor history, exact valuation-date NAVs and eligible fund holdings must exist; otherwise the calculation returns an explicit error.

## HTTP stays explicit

Pass signal for cancellation, timeoutMs for the total request budget and maxRetries for bounded retries. Defaults are 30 seconds and zero retries. Retried mutations require a caller-supplied `idempotencyKey`; cancellation does not imply rollback. The SDK never follows redirects with credentials or caches account responses.

The published package supports named ESM and CommonJS imports under the browser export condition. This is module compatibility, not permission to put account keys in browser code. Browser applications still need an authorized server integration and their own trusted session transport; the private Bharosa adapter is not distributed here.

The SDK is MIT licensed, copyright Bharosa Technoserve Private Limited. This applies only to SDK material; the API and analytics implementation remain closed source. The SDK source is available at https://github.com/bhafin/sdk. Version 0.1.0 is published at https://www.npmjs.com/package/bharosa/v/0.1.0. Publishing the SDK does not activate the API or grant account access.

Use Node.js 22.12 or later in a supported LTS release. ESM and CommonJS entry points expose the same named Bharosa export and types. The examples use the published package name `bharosa`. A clean registry installation and offline runtime checks passed; authenticated live API flows are verified separately.

Every endpoint page includes a cURL alternative with the same path, JSON body and status. Configure the API origin instead of assuming a public domain.
